subject: Urgent: Major latency + 5xx surge — possible transparent proxy / DNS handoff
body:
From: Priya Shah <priya@stellarretail.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike: checkout latency / 502s across west-us region

Hi Rachel,

We started seeing a sudden spike in checkout latency (~1.2s -> 5s p50) and a growing 502/504 rate since ~07:45 PT. This is affecting ~18% of checkout traffic and is causing timeouts in our payment flow.

Quick observations from our side:
- Errors correlate with requests routed to west-us-a (we see higher retry rates).
- DNS lookups for inference.redwood.ai resolved momentarily to an unexpected edge IP (see traceroute).
- We've captured request ids 8f3a2f.. and included a packet capture.

Please advise next steps — this is hitting our SLO and we risk failing a promo tonight.

Attachments: traceroute-stellar-20261101.txt, pcap-sample-1.pcap

Thanks,
Priya Shah
SRE, Stellar Retail
ops@stellarretail.com

-----Original Message-----

From: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai; vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai; jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 08:20:13 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Spike: checkout latency / 502s across west-us region

Folks — forwarding urgent customer report. Priya attached a traceroute and pcap. Can infra/network take a look first? I started a Jira (NET-9132) and linked logs.

Ask: fast triage, identify whether this is an internal path (peering/nat) or external handoff (transparent proxy / partner DNS). If we need to shift routing or open fallback capacity, let me know asap.

Thanks,
Rachel
Account Exec (Strategic)
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: traceroute-stellar-20261101.txt (text/plain)]

On Sun, Nov 1, 2026 at 08:34 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai> wrote:

> From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
> To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai; vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai; jonas.weber@redwood.ai
> Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 08:34:50 -0700
> Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike: checkout latency / 502s across west-us region
>
> Thanks for flagging — I'm on it. Initial checks (08:30 PT):
> - Ingress QPS from Stellar saw a 3.4x jump at 07:46; token validation latency increased concurrently.
> - Host-level metrics on west-us-a show CPU steady; however, connection resets (RST) spiked on our egress proxies.
> - DNS server logs show intermittent TTL mismatches; some lookups returned a third-party edge in the path (not in our catalog).
>
> I pulled the traceroute (attached) and a quick grep of proxy logs. Two hypotheses:
> 1) A transparent proxy (partner or cloud infra) began intercepting/terminating some TLS connections, causing occasional backend 502s; or
> 2) A stale VPC-peering route or asymmetric path causing packets to hit a less-capable NAT/ACL device.
>
> Immediate actions I took:
> - Re-routed a small % of traffic through a reserve egress pool (west-us-b) to test impact (10% diversion).
> - Captured additional proxy logs and increased DNS instrument logging.
> - Opened NET-9132 and dropped our initial findings there.
>
> Can Jonas pull firewall/NAT logs for the peering link and check conntrack exhaustion? Vanessa, can you coordinate with Stellar (Priya) to validate whether their edge changed NXDOMAIN/TTL settings?
>
> - Soojin
>
> [Attachment: soojin-proxy-grep-0832.txt]

On Sun, Nov 1, 2026 at 09:06 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:

> From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
> To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>; rachel.kim@redwood.ai; vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
> Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:06:11 -0700
> Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike: checkout latency / 502s across west-us region
>
> Quick update from NAT/firewall side:
> - No conntrack exhaustion on our aggregate counters, but I see uneven session termination on the peering appliance (peer-id: peer-west-3). The termination timestamps cluster around 07:45-07:50 PT.
> - Firewall policy logs show a surge of SYN retries from an intermediate hop (AS65021) that is not one of our direct peers — looks like a transit provider is in the path.
> - I flagged a possible asymmetric route where return traffic takes a different transit path that traverses a transparent proxy operated by third-party CDN XYZ.
>
> Recommended next steps:
> - Temporarily enable BGP community to prefer our west-us-b egress for Stellar ASN (10%->60% shift) to reduce exposure while we trace the transit path.
> - Request Stellar ops to confirm any outbound DNS changes or CDN failover.
> - Escalate to network ops lead if we see new 5xx once traffic fully reroutes.
>
> I can push the BGP preference change in 10m if we have buy-in.
>
> - Jonas
>
> [Attachment: peer-west-3-firewall-snapshot-0745.log]

On Sun, Nov 1, 2026 at 10:12 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:

> From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
> To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>; Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>; rachel.kim@redwood.ai
> Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 10:12:05 -0700
> Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike: checkout latency / 502s across west-us region
>
> I just spoke with Priya — Stellar confirms they exercised a CDN failover at ~07:40 PT to route traffic through their partner CDN for a regional promo. They didn't expect the partner CDN to act as a transparent TLS terminator for our domains.
>
> They provided a support trace showing the partner using a proxy pool that does TLS interception for certain hostnames when load increases. That matches the asymmetric/transit observation.
>
> Given this, I support Jonas's BGP preference shift. Additional asks:
> - Legal/compliance: confirm whether intercepted TLS (even for performance) violates terms for customers with sensitive workloads.
> - Product: consider pinning customer DNS to our verified edge IPs for critical routes.
>
> I'm pinging our customer success lead to craft a mitigation message for the customer.
>
> - Vanessa
>
> [Attachment: stellar-support-trace-0742.txt]
>
From: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai; vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai; jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Spike: checkout latency / 502s across west-us region — exec summary and next steps

Team — final update and requested exec attention. Chronology & current status:
- 07:40 PT: Stellar initiated CDN failover; partner CDN began intercepting TLS for some hostnames (customer-side decision).
- 07:45–08:00 PT: Our peering path and transit visibility shows asymmetric return path through partner CDN (AS65021).
- 08:30 PT: We diverted 10%->60% traffic to west-us-b; p50 reduced from ~5s to ~1.1s for diverted traffic. Backend 5xx rate stabilized on the diverted pool.

Impact: ~18% of Stellar checkout traffic experienced increased latency/5xx; broad customer impact avoided after partial reroute. However, this is an executive-level customer issue because:
- It was caused by third-party interception of TLS during a customer-initiated failover.
- The customer's commercial/promotional window made this high-severity.

Action items (owner & ETA):
- Network ops (Jonas): Fully prefer west-us-b for Stellar ASN until EOD 2026-11-02. (ETA: 10m for change, completed)
- Infra (Soojin): Continue proxy log capture and validate no residual 502 patterns in west-us-b. (ETA: ongoing, first report 11/01 18:15 PT)
- CS (Vanessa): Coordinate customer comms & confirm if they want remediation assistance with their CDN partner. (ETA: 11/01 19:00 PT)
- Legal/Product: Assess contract/terms implications and propose DNS pinning for critical SLOs. (ETA: 11/02 EOD)

Requesting exec visibility: Please loop in Markus Klein (VP Network Ops) and Priya's counterpart at Stellar if we need credits/compensation. We should also consider a short postmortem with Stellar and their CDN partner to avoid recurrence.

Logs/Artifacts: attached traceroute, support traces, firewall snapshot and SLO heatmap. Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/NET-9132

I'll prepare a short incident brief for leadership after we collect final metrics.

Thanks all for the fast triage.

Rachel Kim
Strategic Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

[Attachments: traceroute-stellar-20261101.txt, slo-heatmap-1101.png, support-logbundle-20261101.tar.gz]
